_: Artifacts that predate provenance recording. This file is a NAMED BACKLOG, not an
exemption: scripts/check_provenance.py prints every entry, by name, on every run, and
an entry stops applying the moment its artifact's digest changes -- regenerate one and
you must record real provenance for it. scripts/check_provenance.py --strict refuses
the backlog entirely.
The four entries with reproduction_attempted=true were checked, not assumed: each was
re-exported from its source tree with the pinned Joern and the committed exporter, and
each DIFFERS. That is the finding, and it is why this file says `unattributed` rather
than quietly recording today's exporter digest against yesterday's artifact -- which
would have made a false claim look like a green check.
ast-Cachetools.json is the one entry whose source revision was RECOVERED rather than
recorded: a fresh export of cachetools v7.1.7 reproduces its exact 209-entry (name,
file) set, which is what identifies the tag. It still DIFFERS in the bodies, so it
stays here -- but its source_hint is now a public tag rather than a dead scratch path.
ast-V8Numbers.json and ast-V8Base.json are the weakest entries in this file and say so:
they name the commit that produced or changed the artifact and nothing about the tree it
came from. A C++ corpus that size cannot be identified by matching a fresh export the way
cachetools was. Do not read them as equivalent to the reproduction_attempted=true entries.
An entry LEAVES this file exactly one way: a real record replaces it. When
scripts/reland_corpus.sh re-exports a corpus from its identified revision it calls
scripts/provenance.py record, which writes provenance/ast-<M>.json.prov.json (joern
version, exporter sha256, artifact digest, source revision, exact command), and then
deletes this file's entry for the same artifact. Both must happen: a record beside a
surviving backlog line makes check_provenance report a digest change against a baseline
that no longer applies. Do not edit an entry's digest by hand to match a regenerated
artifact -- that is the 'stale excuse' the checker's own message warns against.
source_hint paths are per-session scratch directories. They are a lead for whoever
regenerates these, not a stable location, and check_provenance.py does not read them.
The two *Sample entries are a different kind of gap from the rest, and say so: they
are not stale exports, they are EXTRACTIONS. Each is a byte-identical subset of an
untracked corpus AST (verified entry-by-entry against ast-LinuxLib.json and
ast-V8Base.json), and no extraction script is committed, so there is no `command`
that regenerates them and a record naming export_ast.sc + a source tree would be
false. Committing the extractor is what closes these, not a re-export.
